sentences.text:
Case :- Writ - C No. - 44520 of 2023
Petitioner :- Mohd. Shamshad @ Samsad Ahmad

Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Abdul Mateen
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Sanjay Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,Acting Chief Justice
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

The petitioner has challenged the award dated 02.07.2022 passed by the Deputy Land Acquisition
Officer, Maharajganj and the award of Arbitrator/District Magistrate, Maharajganj dated
18.08.2023 under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956.
2.  The case of the petitioner is that the compensation awarded is inadequate as residential and commercial building was standing on the acquired land.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Shri Sanjay Kumar Singh, learned counsel for respondent No. 2, National Highway Authority of India submits that the petitioner has remedy of filing objection against the award of the Arbitrator in terms of sub-section (6) of section 3-G of the National Highways Act, 1956.
4. We find the objection to be valid.

Consequently, we decline to entertain the challenge and relegate the petitioner to the remedy provided under the National Highways Act, 1956 read with provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
5. In case, any objection is filed under the aforesaid provision, it will be examined independently as regards its maintainability and limitation etc. without being influenced by the instant order.
